identification: Python and PowerShell two-vector Windows UAC elevation launchers
evidence: Build hidden PowerShell -NoProfile -File command pointing to a TEMP stage (PowerShell allows an alternate stage argument).
Overwrite HKCU Environment windir with that command plus an ampersand/rem tail; request SilentCleanup execution; wait two seconds; delete windir.
Create the per-user Folder shell open command key, set its default value to the stage command, launch sdclt /KickOffElev, and delete the key.
Both attempts execute sequentially without testing whether the first attempt succeeded. Python ignores child exit status via check=False; PowerShell waits for launchers without checking elevation.
Python performs these operations when the module is loaded. There is no main guard.
limits: The referenced repair.ps1 stage is not included; its behavior and availability cannot be inferred.
No network contact, credential theft, encryption, encoded payload, or downloaded code occurs in either supplied file.
No supplied product metadata, registry package identity, family fingerprint, or authorized-testing wrapper establishes a specific product or research tool identity.
Actual UAC bypass success is Windows-version/configuration dependent and was not tested on Windows.

The sdclt Folder path variant omits DelegateExecute; the published KickOffElev/IsolatedCommand variant uses another registry surface. Treat this as a bypass attempt, not demonstrated high-integrity execution.
The ampersand/rem suffix is not automatically interpreted by PowerShell -File; expansion/argument behavior depends on the scheduled task launch path.
Deleting overrides without preserving previous values can alter pre-existing configuration; exceptions or timing races can leave overrides in place.
method: Full source and parser-fact review; Python execution with registry, process, environment, and sleep calls replaced by recording stubs; PowerShell AST and sequential command/dataflow review. External mechanism descriptions are not sample reputation evidence.
intentional_changes: windir/SilentCleanup conviction requires a command-tail setter, not merely a windir value update.
PowerShell sdclt conviction requires a Folder-key variable bound to Set-Item.
Forced file deletion requires a file-shaped target rather than a provider-neutral Remove-Item command.
Registry-path variable removal is detected under registry/delete.
Windows platform literal no longer matches Windows path fragments.
windir access requires explicit HKCU Environment provider context.
Moves out of process/create intentionally stop generic process-creation directory selectors from consuming mere command options; exact consumers follow relocated IDs.
Python Folder conviction requires SetValueEx on the handle of the created per-user Folder command key; wrong-handle writes do not qualify.

The existing unresolved variable-path deletion fallback excludes proven registry-provider removal and defers to a precise filesystem binding when available. This preserves the keylogger fixture while preventing registry-only false positives.
Require whitespace between the PowerShell executable and options: hyphenated trait names in benign comments are not command invocations. The WAF benign control now forbids that false positive.
controls: 16 source fixtures, including maintenance, wrong handle, reassignment, registry-only, filesystem-only, combined deletion, and positional path arguments.
verification: atomscan rerun on both original paths
Both original SHA-256 values verified unchanged
